written: 2026-10-21, before the full GENCO run on the 15 grids. Disclosure: a mechanics smoke test of run_genco.py on pglib_opf_case14_ieee alone ran before this file (to fix the gen-alignment assertion); its medians were seen (GENCO dVa ~1.95 deg, Pg MAE ~60 MW vs B3 ~0.23 deg / ~16 MW) and nothing in the protocol or code was changed in response. Baseline code was run on 3 case14 scenarios before freezing (oracle reproduces labels to 1e-9).
question: Zero-shot, does the released GENCO pretraining checkpoint infer the state of an unseen grid better than the best classical alternative when loads are known, generator dispatch Pg is UNKNOWN, and |V| is measured at only 20% of buses?
scenarios: graphkit test split of each grid, identical to the 15-grid zero-shot scoring (counts equal results/2026-10-07-genco-heldout-zeroshot n_test_scenarios); ids in test_ids.json
checkpoint: data/external/genco-pf-transfer/pretraining/best_model_state_dict.pt (released), no normalizer file (graphkit default path), no training, no tuning

task_mask.Vm: visible at exactly k=max(1,round(0.2 n)) buses, seeded: numpy default_rng([20261021, n, scenario_id]).permutation(n)[:k]; masked elsewhere
task_mask.Va: masked everywhere except REF; REF Va VISIBLE at its label value (the case's reference angle; decided before the run)

baselines.info: scenario's own Ybus/branch/gen tables, Pd,Qd, type flags, REF angle (label), the CASE FILE (pglib .m: base Pg and Vg per gen, base-case loss fraction from a pandapower AC run), and for B2 the measured |V|. No other label content.
baselines.B1_ac: dispatch = case-file Pg of in-service gens scaled so total = total Pd x (1 + base loss fraction); |V| setpoint at PV/REF = case-file Vg; AC Newton from DC start (tol 1e-8, 30 it); measured |V| ignored; no Q-limit enforcement (as the labels)
baselines.B2_ac_meas: B1, but at measured buses that are PV or REF the |V| setpoint is the measurement
baselines.B3_dc: MATPOWER-style DC power flow (taps, shifters, branch status) with B1's dispatch; |V| = setpoints at PV/REF, 1.0 at PQ
baselines.oracle (control, not a competitor): label bus Pg and label |V| at PV/REF -> must reproduce labels
baselines.non-convergence: B1/B2 that do not converge fall back to the B3 DC state and are flagged converged=false (counted in the report)

controls: oracle-dispatch AC solve reproduces labels (max |dVa|, |dVm| over all scenarios reported)
genco_det100: same checkpoint, Vm visible at 100% of buses (upper-ish reference for the angle and Pg metrics; its Vm metric is empty)
visible entries pass through GENCO unchanged (diag vm_visible_dev, va_ref_dev logged per grid)

metric_defs.dva_mae: per scenario: mean over in-service branches of |wrap((va_f - va_t)_pred - (va_f - va_t)_label)| (deg)
metric_defs.vm_mae_unmeas: per scenario: mean over buses NOT in the measured set of ||V|_pred - |V|_label| (pu)
metric_defs.pg_mae: per scenario: mean over in-service generators of |Pg_pred - Pg_label| (MW)

statistic: per grid: median over test scenarios of the per-scenario MAE; ratio = GENCO median / min over eligible baselines of their medians (best baseline re-selected inside every bootstrap resample, which is conservative for GENCO)

bootstrap.unit: scenario, resampled with replacement, same scenarios for all methods

win_rule: GENCO wins a metric on a grid iff ratio < 1 AND the bootstrap 95% CI upper bound < 1; wins the grid iff it wins BOTH primary metrics
verdict_rule: PASS iff GENCO wins the grid on >= 10 of 15 grids; else FAIL. Pg MAE is secondary and reported only; it does not change the verdict.
also_reported_not_in_verdict: wins at the point estimate without the CI rule
